items.title: Mub-completeness, mub-closure, Plotkin orders, and bifinite domains
items.summary: Mub-completeness, mub-closure, Plotkin orders, and bifinite domains.
items.reviewNote: All five source components are selectable. The reusable mub and compact-basis predicates remain defined over OrderedDomain's Preorder carrier, while IsBifiniteCategoryObject now restores the dcpo and antisymmetry assumptions implicit in the textbook's category B. A future PartialOrder-based core refactor is still pending.

items.title: Bifinite-to-pointed-algebraic function spaces are algebraic
items.summary: Bifinite-to-pointed-algebraic function spaces are algebraic.
items.reviewNote: The constructive proof sketch is formalized: finite compact observations are closed under compact-basis minimal upper bounds, refined to monotone compact labels, converted to joinable families, and shown to form a directed basis below each continuous map. The numbered proposition contains no local sorry or admit; it depends on Lemma 4.2.3, whose proof is omitted by the textbook and remains an explicit admit.

items.title: Mub-complete algebraic bases yield least kernel operators fixing compact sets
items.summary: Mub-complete algebraic bases yield least kernel operators fixing compact sets.
items.reviewNote: The source proof is fully reconstructed: mub-completeness makes each generated lower section directed, dcpo completeness defines its supremum, Corollary 2.2.16 gives Scott continuity, and algebraicity shows every competing kernel fixing A also fixes mc(A). The signature explicitly supplies dcpo completeness and antisymmetry because the current local OrderedDomain/IsAlgebraicDomain interfaces do not bundle those textbook assumptions.

items.title: Functional characterizations of bifinite domains by idempotent deflations
items.summary: Functional characterizations of bifinite domains by idempotent deflations.
items.reviewNote: The full equivalence is proved. Finite mub-closures generate finite projections; these form a directed family with pointwise supremum the identity. Conversely, directed finite projections give an algebraic basis, mub-completeness, finite mub-closures, and hence a Plotkin compact basis. The all-deflations formulation follows by choosing a family member fixing the finite union of two projection ranges.

items.title: Bifinite domains are exactly bilimits of expanding systems of finite pointed posets
items.summary: Bifinite domains are exactly bilimits of expanding systems of finite pointed posets.
items.reviewNote: The theorem now uses an arbitrary directed index type rather than a Nat-indexed sequence. The forward proof takes the finite kernel images of the directed idempotent deflations supplied by Theorem 4.2.6; the reverse proof composes each finite-stage projection with its embedding and applies the functional characterization. The explicit antisymmetry hypothesis reflects that OrderedDomain currently bundles only a Preorder.

items.title: The category of bifinite domains is cartesian closed and closed under listed constructions
items.summary: The category of bifinite domains is cartesian closed and closed under listed constructions.
items.reviewNote: Product closure and the textbook's function-space proof are now formalized through directed finite projections; in particular the finite image and double directed-supremum arguments for h ↦ g_j ∘ h ∘ f_i are proved. The elementary coalesced-sum clause has no proof details in the textbook and remains admit; bilimit closure remains admit because the textbook explicitly leaves it as an exercise. The cartesian-closed conclusion still uses the local object-closure interface rather than categorical universal properties.

items.reviewNote: The source explicitly says the proof is as yet unknown. Lean therefore defines only the proposition-valued statement and exposes no theorem, axiom, admit, or sorry evidence for it. The old source-number name remains only as a proposition-valued compatibility abbreviation. No downstream proof may consume this claim.

The textbook-omitted coalesced-sum proof remains admit, and cartesian closedness is still represented only by object closure.

items.summary: Continuous function-space separation: coherent domain or L-domain codomain.

The exercise is an admit because the textbook explicitly omits it. The only source-case sorry is isolated in the Figure 12 branch: the printed successor construction and pointwise-supremum claim require source-valid chain data not present in the displayed diagram. Proposition 4.2.16 is also a tracked transitive dependency.

items.title: Bottomed continuous domains are FS iff self-function coherence conditions hold
items.summary: Bottomed continuous domains are FS iff self-function coherence conditions hold.
items.reviewNote: Jung [Jun90, Corollary 2.2.14] was located and checked. Its Lawson-compact implication is recorded as an exact external axiom. The forward direction now uses Jun90 Theorem 2.2.6 together with a proved local theorem that every FS object is continuous; it deliberately does not use the conjectural Proposition 4.2.10. Remaining debt is only in explicitly tracked dependencies.
